subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: Should terminal config-validation errors print effective received values, and if so must confidentiality be determined from schema/plugin metadata rather than the current path-name heuristic?
rationale: This choice controls whether arbitrary plugin-owned configuration values may reach terminal output and also determines which overlapping implementation should become canonical.

options.title: Require schema-aware disclosure
options.body: Keep received-value hints only after the branch uses effective validation values and a closed, owner-approved sensitivity contract covering plugin-owned fields.

options.title: Defer received values
options.body: Land bracket paths and line locations through the canonical formatter while omitting received-value output until the confidentiality contract is designed.

options.title: Accept heuristic filtering
options.body: Allow the current path-based filtering policy and explicitly own the possibility that unclassified custom fields appear in terminal diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Require schema-aware disclosure
recommendation.body: Keep received-value hints only after the branch uses effective validation values and a closed, owner-approved sensitivity contract covering plugin-owned fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans central configuration UX, plugin-owned config boundaries, and terminal disclosure policy, all adjacent to this contributor's recent config-area work.
